title: Meet North Micro Vision: A 2.4B Native-Resolution Vision-Language Model
gist: Cohere Labs released North-Micro-Vision-Instruct, a 2.4B-parameter Apache 2.0 vision-language model pairing a custom 400M native-resolution SigLIP-2-derived encoder with an in-house 2B Command A+-architecture LLM, trained on an OCR/document-heavy four-stage curriculum. The published benchmark table shows it winning on document understanding (DocVQA 0.921) and visual grounding (RefCOCO avg 0.732) while losing badly on STEM and text-only reasoning (MMMU 0.329, MMLU 0.504) to similarly sized rivals — an explicit bet on narrow document/edge deployment over general intelligence.

themes.theme: Compact open-weight release and sovereign-AI positioning

insights.claim: Cohere Labs released North-Micro-Vision-Instruct, a 2.4B-parameter open-weight vision-language model with native-resolution image support under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Another frontier-adjacent lab pushing sub-3B multimodal weights out under Apache 2.0 further commoditizes the small-VLM tier and pressures pricing for hosted vision APIs.

insights.claim: Cohere frames this model release as part of a 'sovereign AI' strategy, explicitly bundling open weights, clear licensing and transparent evaluation as the product rather than raw capability.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Sovereignty/auditability is becoming the differentiating sales axis for non-US-hyperscaler AI vendors selling into governments and regulated enterprises.
insights.quote: The release reflects Cohere's broader work on sovereign AI by pairing model development with clear licensing, open weights, and transparent evaluation.
insights.locator: The release reflects Cohere's broader work

insights.claim: The 2.4B parameter scale is pitched as the point where vision-language inference escapes server-only deployment and moves onto laptops and mobile-class hardware given the right inference stack and quantization.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Confirms the sub-3B VLM tier as the battleground for on-device multimodal apps, favouring edge silicon and inference-runtime vendors over cloud GPU rental for this workload.
insights.quote: With the right inference stack and quantization, models at this scale can also support experimentation beyond server-only deployments, including on laptops and edge or mobile-class hardware.
insights.locator: North Micro Vision is our smallest VLM to date

insights.claim: Cohere shipped North Micro Vision before public vLLM support existed, evaluating it with an internal vLLM implementation instead — a sign that model release cadence is now outrunning open-source serving-stack integration.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Benchmarks published against private inference stacks are hard to reproduce; treat day-one numbers from any lab shipping ahead of vLLM/llama.cpp support as provisional.

themes.theme: Architecture: native resolution and hybrid attention

insights.claim: North Micro Vision combines a custom-trained 400M-parameter native-resolution vision encoder with an in-house 2B-parameter language model called North Micro LLM, rather than adapting an off-the-shelf open LLM backbone.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Vertical control of both encoder and LLM lets Cohere ship licence-clean weights without inheriting a third party's restrictions — a structural advantage for sovereignty-driven customers.
insights.locator: North Micro Vision combines a custom-trained 400M-parameter

insights.claim: The language model follows Cohere's Command A+ architecture, interleaving three sliding-window attention layers using rotary positional embeddings with one global attention layer that has no positional embeddings at all.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: The 3:1 local-to-global hybrid attention pattern is converging as the industry default for long-context efficiency; watch it propagate into inference-kernel and KV-cache optimisation products.
insights.quote: interleaving three sliding-window attention layers that use rotary positional embeddings with one global attention layer without positional embeddings
insights.locator: The language model follows our Command A+ architecture

insights.claim: Rather than feeding visual features only at the input layer, the projector follows DeepStack and injects patch embeddings from multiple vision-encoder layers into corresponding early LLM layers, giving the LLM visual representations at several levels of abstraction.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Multi-level visual injection is a cheap architectural lever for small VLMs to punch above their parameter count on fine-detail tasks — a pattern to expect in competing sub-3B releases.
insights.quote: patch embeddings from multiple vision-encoder layers are injected into corresponding early LLM layers
insights.locator: The projector maps visual features into the language model's embedding space

insights.claim: The vision encoder was continued-pretrained from Google's public SigLIP 2 SO400M checkpoint using Continual Rotary Position Embedding, combining 2D RoPE with bilinearly interpolated learned 1D positional embeddings to support native-resolution inputs.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Even labs building their own LLMs still bootstrap vision from Google's open SigLIP checkpoints — Google retains quiet upstream influence over the entire open VLM stack.
insights.locator: We continued pre-training the vision encoder from the SigLIP 2 SO400M checkpoint

themes.theme: Four-stage training curriculum and resolution ladder

insights.claim: The vision-encoder curriculum stepped resolution from 384x384 (10M examples, LLM frozen) to 1024x1024 (13M examples, joint training) to a 1654x2339 native-resolution cap (10M examples), the final stage corresponding to a full A4 page at 200 dpi.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Designing the resolution ceiling around a scanned A4 page reveals the target market is document/back-office automation, not consumer photo understanding.
insights.quote: corresponding to an A4 page at 200 dpi

insights.claim: The pre-training data mixture was deliberately OCR-heavy — 60% dense captions and 40% OCR in stage 1, then an even 50/50 caption/OCR split through both higher-resolution stages.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Data-mix disclosure at this granularity is rare and gives competitors a directly copyable recipe for document-specialised small VLMs.

insights.claim: The 50M-example instruction-tuning mixture was dominated by document-style tasks — native OCR 17.8%, charts and tables 17.8%, grounding and counting 13.3%, OCR QA 13.3% — while reserving 8.9% for text-only data to prevent language degradation.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Only ~9% text-only retention explains the model's weak MMLU scores — a quantified illustration of the multimodal-vs-text capacity tradeoff at small scale.

insights.claim: Longer native-resolution instruction training produced the largest gains specifically in document understanding and visual grounding, because those tasks depend on preserving small text, layout details and precise spatial information.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Native resolution is the mechanism behind document-VLM performance, so any competitor still downsampling to fixed squares is structurally disadvantaged in enterprise document workloads.
insights.quote: with the largest gains in document understanding and visual grounding

insights.claim: For final preference tuning Cohere simplified Mixed Preference Optimization by dropping the BCO quality loss entirely, combining DPO with an auxiliary SFT loss weighted at 15% relative to DPO, and freezing the vision encoder and projector so only the language model updated across 500k examples.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: A published simplification of a standard alignment recipe lowers the compute bar for smaller labs doing multimodal preference tuning.

insights.claim: Cohere found that once the lowest-scoring training examples were removed by an internal judging pipeline, applying increasingly aggressive quality thresholds had only a marginal effect on final model performance.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Undercuts the 'data quality is everything' narrative at the margin — spend on coverage and curation breadth beats ever-finer filtering, which caps the value of premium data-cleaning vendors.
insights.quote: After we removed the lowest-scoring data, applying increasingly aggressive thresholds had only a marginal effect on final performance.

insights.claim: Small changes to the training data recipe produced no large performance differences as long as the mixture stayed balanced across capabilities, languages and domains, implying that mixture proportions are a weak lever compared with breadth of coverage.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Reduces the perceived moat from secret data-mixture ratios; the defensible asset is the underlying multilingual document corpus, not the blend.
insights.quote: coverage and balance mattered more than narrowly tuning the proportions

insights.claim: The curriculum leaned on an in-house, large-scale multilingual document corpus used to synthesise OCR, chart-understanding, HTML-table-generation and grounding data across languages, alongside public datasets.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Proprietary document corpora plus synthesis pipelines are the real scarce input in document VLMs — a durable advantage over labs relying only on public data.

themes.theme: Benchmark profile: document/grounding wins, STEM and text losses

insights.claim: North-Micro-Vision-Instruct scores 0.921 on DocVQA VAL, beating Ministral-3-3B-Instruct (0.896), Phi-3.5-vision-instruct (0.860), Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (0.825) and Gemma-4-E2B-it (0.732), and trailing only Qwen3.5-2B-Instruct at 0.926.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Document extraction quality at 2.4B is now near-saturated across vendors, so document-AI startups charging for OCR accuracy alone are losing their technical moat.

insights.claim: On grounding, North Micro Vision's RefCOCO average of 0.732 dwarfs Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct (0.304), Ministral-3-3B-Instruct (0.317), Phi-3.5-vision-instruct (0.451) and Gemma-4-E2B-it (0.084), showing that spatial grounding remains wildly uneven across compact VLMs rather than commoditized.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Grounding is the differentiating capability for UI-agent and robotics use cases; the 0.08-to-0.79 spread means model choice materially decides whether those products work at all.

insights.claim: The model's STEM reasoning is its clearest weakness: MMMU DEV_VAL of 0.329 sits well below Ministral-3-3B-Instruct (0.508), Gemma-4-E2B-it (0.477) and even SmolVLM2.2B (0.399).
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Buyers must segment small VLMs by task: this one is a document/grounding workhorse, not a reasoning engine, and marketing that conflates the two should be discounted.

insights.claim: Text-only capability was sacrificed for vision: North Micro Vision scores 0.504 on MMLU and 0.307 on MMLU-Pro versus 0.692 and 0.441 for Gemma-4-E2B-it and 0.660 and 0.475 for Ministral-3-3B-Instruct.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: A quantified multimodal tax at small scale — deployments needing both text and vision will still run two models, keeping aggregate inference demand higher than headline parameter counts suggest.

insights.claim: Cohere disclosed that comparison models were evaluated under each vendor's own recommended inference settings within VLMEvalKit with generation capped at 1,024 tokens and reasoning models excluded, an unusually explicit methodology statement for a launch post.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: Methodology transparency is becoming a competitive signal in open-model releases; opaque launch benchmarks should be treated as marketing.

insights.claim: Cohere shipped an NVIDIA AutoModel recipe in partnership with NVIDIA at launch so developers can fine-tune and deploy North Micro Vision on NVIDIA GPUs out of the box, alongside community MLX-VLM weights and Axolotl fine-tuning support.
insights.speaker: David Rau
insights.so_what: NVIDIA continues to co-market every credible open-weight release, reinforcing CUDA as the default fine-tuning substrate even for models aimed at edge and Apple silicon.
